mainTopic: A one-day-old baby's full legal status, and the פסוקים behind each of the משנה's rules about him
overview: This amud opens with the end of the משנה: a one-day-old baby boy already has full legal standing. He inherits and passes on an inheritance, killing him is murder, and his family mourns him fully. The גמרא then finds a פסוק for each rule. The extra ו in 'וְאִשָּׁה' brings baby girls into נדה and זיבה. For a baby boy as a זב, רבי יהודה learns from the doubled 'אִישׁ אִישׁ', while רבי ישמעאל learns from 'לַזָּכָר' and says the doubling is just normal speech (דברה תורה כלשון בני אדם). Short sources follow for נגעים, טומאת מת, יבום, and a baby's effect on his mother's right to eat תרומה. The גמרא explains why the תורה needs both 'no child' and 'as in her youth', and רב ששת explains why the משנה says 'one day old' rather than a fetus. Finally, רב ששת explains that the baby inherits his mother and passes her property to his brothers from his father, which a fetus cannot do. That last explanation finishes on the next amud.

steps.title: A one-day-old baby has full legal standing
steps.stepSummary: The משנה finishes its list of laws that already apply to a one-day-old baby boy: inheritance, liability for murder, and full mourning.
steps.simpleTranslation: He inherits and passes on an inheritance. Someone who kills him is liable. To his father, his mother, and all his relatives he is like a complete groom.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the end of the משנה. It teaches that even a one-day-old baby boy counts as a full person for inheritance, murder, and mourning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה is not just saying a baby can become טמא. It is saying a newborn is a complete person in the eyes of הלכה. He can inherit from his mother, his heirs can inherit from him, killing him is a capital crime, and his family mourns him as fully as they would a grown man.

keyTerms.meaning: He inherits, and he passes the inheritance on to his heirs
One who kills him is liable for murder
A complete groom, meaning a grown man whose death is fully mourned
His relatives

steps.whatToRemember: A one-day-old baby is a full person in הלכה. He inherits, killing him is murder, and he is fully mourned.

phrases.english: And he inherits and bequeaths,
and one who kills him is liable,
and he is, to his father and to his mother
and to all his relatives, like a full-fledged groom.
phrases.notes: This is about mourning: his family mourns him as fully as they would a grown, married man.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: A one-day-old baby inherits, bequeaths, is protected by murder liability, and is mourned like a full adult.

steps.title: Where do we learn that a newborn girl can be a נדה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens by asking for the source of the משנה's rule that a one-day-old girl can become a נדה.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: From where are these words learned?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins and asks for the פסוק behind the משנה's first rule, that a one-day-old girl can become טמאה as a נדה. This sets up the ברייתא that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה speaks about an 'אִשָּׁה', a woman, so it is not obvious that a baby girl is included. The גמרא wants a source before accepting the משנה's rule.

keyTerms.meaning: The discussion section that analyzes the משנה
From where are these words learned? A request for the scriptural source

phrases.english: GEMARA: From where are these matters derived?
phrases.notes: He's asking about the משנה's first rule, that a one-day-old girl can become a נדה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from the משנה to asking for its scriptural source.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The פסוק showing that נדה applies even to a one-day-old girl.

steps.title: The extra ו in וְאִשָּׁה includes a baby girl for נדה
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא shows that the word 'וְאִשָּׁה' with its extra ו includes a one-day-old girl in the laws of נדה.
steps.simpleTranslation: As the רבנן taught: 'A woman.' This only gives me a grown woman. From where do we learn that a one-day-old girl can be a נדה? The פסוק says 'And a woman.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its question with a ברייתא. The extra letter ו ('and') in the פסוק is read as adding a one-day-old girl.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The plain word 'אִשָּׁה' would only mean a grown woman. The extra ו at the start of 'וְאִשָּׁה' is read as a hint that something more is included, and that something is a baby girl. This is a classic way of learning from the wording of a פסוק.

keyTerms.meaning: I would only have, meaning the plain word alone would only teach this much
The פסוק teaches us by saying...
A woman made טמאה by her regular monthly bleeding
'And a woman.' The extra ו adds a further case

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the word 'אִשָּׁה' by itself includes babies. The ברייתא says the opposite: 'אִשָּׁה' alone means a grown woman. Only the extra ו brings in the baby.

phrases.english: As the Sages taught: "A woman"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 15:19

phrases.english: I have only a woman,
from where do I derive a one-day-old girl for menstrual impurity?
The verse states: "And a woman."
phrases.notes: The extra 'and' at the start of the word is what brings in the baby girl.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 2 with a ברייתא.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The extra ו in 'וְאִשָּׁה' includes a one-day-old girl for נדה.

steps.title: Where do we learn that a ten-day-old girl can be a זבה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's next rule, that a ten-day-old girl can become a זבה, and asks for its source.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ten-day-old girl for זיבה: from where are these words learned?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the משנה's next rule and asks again for the source. This sets up a second ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: זיבה is bleeding outside the normal seven days of נדה. A baby needs to be at least ten days old to have three days of bleeding after her first seven, so the משנה gives the age of ten. The גמרא now wants to know how we know זיבה applies to a baby at all.

keyTerms.meaning: Bleeding outside the regular נדה days, which makes a woman a זבה
A ten-day-old girl
From where are these words learned? (the same question as before, slightly different spelling)

phrases.english: A ten-day-old girl for ziva impurity —
from where are these matters derived?

steps.triggerLanguage: בַּת עֲשָׂרָה יָמִים לְזִיבָה מְנָא הָנֵי מִילֵּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Parallel to step 2, now for the משנה's זיבה rule.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The פסוק showing that זיבה applies to a ten-day-old girl.

steps.title: The same extra ו includes a baby girl for זיבה
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא uses the same reasoning on the פסוק about זבה: the extra ו in 'וְאִשָּׁה' includes a ten-day-old girl.
steps.simpleTranslation: As the רבנן taught: 'A woman.' This only gives me a grown woman. From where do we learn that a ten-day-old girl can be a זבה? The פסוק says 'And a woman.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a ברייתא that copies the pattern of step 3, now on the פסוק about זבה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק about זבה also begins 'וְאִשָּׁה', with an extra ו. Just like with נדה, that extra letter is read as including a baby girl. The only difference is which פסוק is being read and the age of the baby.

keyTerms.meaning: A woman who is טמאה because of זיבה bleeding
An inclusion, meaning an extra word or letter that adds a case

steps.whatToRemember: The same tool, the extra ו in 'וְאִשָּׁה', brings baby girls into both נדה and זיבה, each from its own פסוק.

phrases.english: As the Sages taught: "A woman"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 15:25

phrases.english: I have only a woman,
from where do I derive a ten-day-old girl for ziva impurity?
The verse states: "And a woman."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 4, using the same reading as step 3.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The extra ו in 'וְאִשָּׁה' in the זבה passage includes a ten-day-old girl.

steps.title: Where do we learn that a newborn boy can be a זב?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's rule about a one-day-old baby boy and asks for its source.
steps.simpleTranslation: A one-day-old baby boy, etc. From where are these words learned?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now turns to the boy in the משנה and asks how we know a one-day-old boy can become טמא as a זב. This sets up a third ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק about a זב speaks of an 'אִישׁ', a man. So the same problem comes up: how can a newborn boy be included in a law written about a man?

keyTerms.meaning: A baby (here, a baby boy)
Etc. The rest of the משנה's line is understood
A male who is טמא because of an unusual discharge

phrases.english: A one-day-old baby boy, etc.
From where are these matters derived?

steps.triggerLanguage: תִּינוֹק בֶּן יוֹם אֶחָד כּוּ׳ מְנָא הָנֵי מִילֵּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Third parallel question, now about a baby boy.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The פסוק showing that a one-day-old boy can become a זב.

steps.title: The doubled אִישׁ אִישׁ includes a newborn boy for זיבה
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא reads the doubled words 'אִישׁ אִישׁ' as including a one-day-old boy in זיבה. This is the view of רבי יהודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: As the רבנן taught: 'Any man (אִישׁ אִישׁ).' Why does the פסוק say 'אִישׁ אִישׁ'? To include a one-day-old boy, who becomes טמא through זיבה. These are the words of רבי יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a ברייתא. The double word 'אִישׁ אִישׁ' is extra, so it is read as including a newborn boy. רבי יהודה is named as the one who says this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the extra wording is not a ו but a repeated word. One 'אִישׁ' would have been enough, so the second one is read as adding a baby boy. The ending 'דברי רבי יהודה' marks this as one תנא's opinion, which suggests other views may follow.

keyTerms.meaning: Literally 'a man, a man', meaning 'any man'. The doubled word adds a case
Why does the פסוק say this? A sign that the wording is extra
To include
Becomes טמא

steps.whatToRemember: Girls are included through the extra ו in 'וְאִשָּׁה'. A boy is included through the doubled 'אִישׁ אִישׁ', according to רבי יהודה.

phrases.english: As the Sages taught: "Any man"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 15:2

phrases.english: Why must the verse state "any man"?
phrases.notes: Literally 'a man, a man'. One 'man' would have been enough, so the doubled word is extra.

phrases.english: To include a one-day-old boy
that he becomes impure with ziva,
this is the statement of Rabbi Yehuda.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 6, using a doubled word instead of an extra ו.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The doubled 'אִישׁ אִישׁ' includes a one-day-old boy in זיבה, according to רבי יהודה.

steps.title: A different source: 'male or female' includes any age
steps.stepSummary: רבי ישמעאל בנו של רבי יוחנן בן ברוקא says the derivation from 'איש איש' is not needed. The words 'לזכר ולנקבה' already include males and females of any age.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ישמעאל, son of רבי יוחנן בן ברוקא, says: You do not need that. The פסוק says 'and the one with a discharge, whether male or female.' 'Male' means any male, adult or child. 'Female' means any female, adult or child.
steps.whatsHappening: The same ברייתא now brings a second opinion that disagrees with רבי יהודה about where the rule comes from. It finds the source in a different פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה learned from the doubled words 'איש איש' that even a one-day-old boy can become a זב. רבי ישמעאל says this is unnecessary, because 'לזכר' and 'לנקבה' are broad words with no age limit. The rule stays the same. Only its source in the פסוק changes.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not needed. The other derivation is unnecessary.
A man who has a certain kind of discharge that makes him טמא
Anyone at all, with no limit
Adult / minor (child)

steps.confusionAlert: Both sides agree that a baby boy can become a זב. They only argue about which words in the פסוק teach it.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל בְּנוֹ שֶׁל רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן בְּרוֹקָא אוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yishmael, son of Rabbi Yochanan ben Beroka, says:
It is not necessary,
phrases.notes: He means you don't need the extra 'איש' from the last step to teach this.

phrases.aramaic: הֲרֵי הוּא אוֹמֵר: ״וְהַזָּב אֶת זוֹבוֹ לַזָּכָר וְלַנְּקֵבָה״,
phrases.english: for it says: 'And the one with a discharge, whether male or female,'
phrases.notes: ויקרא 15:33

phrases.english: 'male' means anyone who is a male,
whether an adult or a minor;
'female' means anyone who is a female,
whether an adult or a minor.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different source for the same rule that רבי יהודה derived in Step 7.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The words 'לזכר ולנקבה' include males and females of any age, so a one-day-old boy can become a זב.

steps.title: Then why does the Torah say 'man, man'?
steps.stepSummary: If 'לזכר' already teaches the rule, the doubled 'איש איש' seems to have no purpose.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, why does the פסוק say 'איש איש' (any man)?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ישמעאל raises the obvious problem with his own view. Now the doubled words seem extra and unexplained. This sets up his answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually an extra or doubled word in the תורה is read as teaching something new. If 'איש איש' does not teach about babies, it needs another explanation.

keyTerms.meaning: If so, meaning if your view is correct
Why does the פסוק need to say this?
Literally 'man, man'. It means 'any man'.

phrases.aramaic: אִם כֵּן מָה תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר ״אִישׁ אִישׁ״?
phrases.english: If so, why does the verse say 'any man'?
phrases.notes: These are the doubled words רבי יהודה used in Step 7.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the view in Step 8 by asking what the doubled 'איש איש' is for.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי ישמעאל's claim that 'לזכר' is the source
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If 'לזכר' teaches the rule, then 'איש איש' seems to be an extra word with no purpose.

steps.title: The Torah speaks the way people speak
steps.stepSummary: The doubled 'איש איש' is just a normal way of talking. No law is learned from it.
steps.simpleTranslation: The תורה spoke in the language of people.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ישמעאל answers the problem. Doubling a word like 'איש איש' is ordinary speech, so nothing special is learned from it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה reads the doubled word as a hint that adds a new law. רבי ישמעאל says people naturally repeat words for emphasis, and the תורה wrote that way too. So the doubling is not a source for any law.

keyTerms.meaning: The תורה spoke in the normal way people speak, so we do not learn laws from ordinary word repetition.

steps.whatToRemember: There are two sources for a one-day-old boy being a זב. רבי יהודה learns it from 'איש איש'. רבי ישמעאל learns it from 'לזכר', and he says 'איש איש' is just normal speech: דברה תורה כלשון בני אדם.
steps.whyThisMatters: 'דברה תורה כלשון בני אדם' is a basic rule of reading the תורה that appears in many places in ש״ס. It decides when doubled words can be used to learn laws.

phrases.english: The Torah spoke in the language of people.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in Step 9.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rule of reading the פסוק: the doubling is ordinary speech, so nothing is learned from it
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Every doubled word must teach a law, so 'איש איש' would have to be the source.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'איש איש' is normal human speech, and the law comes from 'לזכר'.

steps.title: A baby can become טמא with נגעים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's rule that a one-day-old baby can become טמא with נגעים. The source is the word 'אדם', which has no age limit.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: 'And he becomes טמא with נגעים.' This is because it is written: 'When a person has on the skin of his flesh.' 'A person' means anyone at all.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the משנה's next rule and gives its source right away. It does not ask 'from where do we know this' out loud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק about נגעים uses the general word 'אדם' (a person). Since it does not say 'an adult', it includes anyone, even a baby who is one day old.

keyTerms.meaning: Skin marks (often translated 'leprosy') that can make a person טמא
A person. A general word with no age limit.

phrases.english: And he becomes impure with leprous marks.
As it is written: 'When a person shall have in the skin of his flesh'
phrases.notes: ויקרא 13:2

phrases.english: 'A person' means anyone at all.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next rule in the משנה's list about a one-day-old baby.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The word 'אדם' in ויקרא 13:2 includes a person of any age.

steps.title: A baby can become טמא from a dead body
steps.stepSummary: The rule that a one-day-old baby becomes טמא from a dead body comes from the word 'הנפשות' (the people) in the פסוק about sprinkling.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: 'And he becomes טמא with טומאת מת.' This is because it is written: 'And upon the people who were there.' A 'person' means anyone at all.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next rule in the משנה and gives its source. It follows the same pattern as the last step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says the water is sprinkled on 'the people who were there' in the tent with the dead body. 'נפש' (a person) has no age limit, so a baby in the tent also becomes טמא and needs sprinkling.

keyTerms.meaning: The טומאה a person gets from a dead body
A person, a living soul
Anyone at all. Aramaic for כל שהוא.

phrases.english: And he becomes impure with impurity from a corpse.
As it is written: 'And upon the people who were there'
phrases.notes: במדבר 19:18

phrases.english: A person means anyone at all.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues down the משנה's list with the next rule.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The word 'הנפשות' in במדבר 19:18 includes a person of any age.

steps.title: A baby can create a bond of יבום
steps.stepSummary: The rule that a one-day-old baby creates a bond of יבום comes from 'when brothers dwell together'. This means brothers who were alive in the world at the same time.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: 'And he creates a bond of יבום.' This is because it is written: 'When brothers dwell together.' This means brothers who shared one time of living in the world.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the source for the next rule in the משנה's list: even a one-day-old brother creates a bond of יבום with his dead brother's widow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Dwell together' does not mean living in the same house. It means being alive in the world at the same moment. So a baby born at any point before his brother died, even on that same day, counts as a brother for יבום.

keyTerms.meaning: Creates a bond that ties the widow to him for יבום
Levirate marriage: a man marries his brother's widow when the brother died without children
One dwelling in the world. They were alive at the same time.

steps.confusionAlert: 'Dwelling together' here does not mean the brothers lived in one house. It only means both were alive at the same time, even for one day.
steps.whatToRemember: Each of the משנה's rules about a young baby has its own פסוק. Many rest on a word with no age limit, like 'לזכר', 'אדם', 'נפש', or 'אחים יחדו', while others come from an extra ו or a doubled word.

phrases.english: And he creates a bond for levirate marriage.
As it is written: 'If brothers dwell together'
phrases.notes: דברים 25:5

phrases.english: brothers who had
one dwelling in the world.
phrases.notes: He means they were both alive at the same time, even if only for one day.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for the next rule in the משנה's list.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'כי ישבו אחים יחדו' means brothers who were alive at the same time, which includes a one-day-old baby.

steps.title: A one-day-old son frees his mother from levirate marriage
steps.stepSummary: The rule that a one-day-old baby exempts his widowed mother from יבום comes from 'and he has no son'. Here the dead man does have a son.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says a one-day-old baby exempts his mother from יבום. The תורה says יבום applies when the dead man 'has no son', and this man does have a son.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next rule in the משנה's list and gives its source. A baby only one day old is enough to free the widow from יבום.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק makes יבום depend on the dead brother having no son. It sets no minimum age, so a son born even one day before his father died counts as having a son. That means there is no יבום.

keyTerms.meaning: Exempts, frees from an obligation
The Merciful One, meaning the Torah
But this one does have (it)

phrases.english: And he exempts from levirate marriage.
"And he has no son", the Merciful One said,
phrases.notes: דברים 25:5

phrases.english: and this one does have one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the series of sources for each rule about a one-day-old baby. The previous step gave the source for creating a bond of יבום, and this step gives the source for exempting from it.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What is the source that a one-day-old son exempts his mother from יבום?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'And he has no son' (דברים 25:5). Any son, even one day old, means the dead man has a son.

steps.title: A one-day-old son lets his mother keep eating תרומה
steps.stepSummary: An Israelite mother whose son is a כהן may keep eating תרומה through him, even when he is one day old. The source is reading 'they will eat' as 'they will feed'.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says a one-day-old baby lets his mother eat תרומה. The פסוק says 'those born in his house, they will eat of his bread.' Read it as 'they will feed others of his bread.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the source for the next rule. A newborn son who is a כהן allows his Israelite mother to keep eating תרומה after his father is gone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The plain פסוק says people born in a כהן's house may eat תרומה. By reading the word with different vowels, יַאֲכִילוּ instead of יֹאכְלוּ, the פסוק also teaches that those born to the כהן can make others eat. So the baby, even at one day old, keeps his mother's right to תרומה.

keyTerms.meaning: Makes someone eat, gives them the right to eat
The portion of produce given to a כֹּהֵן, which only כֹּהֲנִים and their households may eat
One born in his house
Read into it, meaning read the word with different vowels to learn an extra lesson

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not saying the baby himself eats תרומה here. The point is that the baby gives his mother the right to eat.

phrases.english: And he enables eating terumah.
As it is written: "And those born in his house,"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 22:11

phrases.english: "they will eat of his bread";
read into it: "they will feed of his bread."

steps.title: A one-day-old son stops his mother from eating תרומה
steps.stepSummary: A בת כהן who married a ישראל may go back to eating תרומה only if she has no child. A one-day-old child is enough to stop her.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says a one-day-old baby disqualifies his mother from תרומה. The תורה says 'and she has no child', and this woman does have a child.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the source for the opposite case. Here the baby takes away his mother's right to תרומה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A בת כהן married to a ישראל loses תרומה. If she is widowed or divorced, the פסוק lets her return to her father's house and eat again, but only if she 'has no child'. A child of any age, even one day old, blocks her return.

keyTerms.meaning: Disqualifies
Offspring, a child
Daughter of a כֹּהֵן

phrases.english: And he disqualifies from terumah.
"And she has no child", the Merciful One said,
phrases.notes: ויקרא 22:13

phrases.english: and this one does have one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Next rule in the list. It is the mirror image of the previous step: there the baby gives the right to eat, and here he takes it away.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What is the source that a one-day-old child disqualifies his mother, a בת כהן, from תרומה?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'And she has no child' (ויקרא 22:13). She has a child, so she cannot return to eat.

steps.title: Why does the פסוק need 'no child' if 'as in her youth' already excludes a pregnant woman?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks about the פסוק. Why does the תורה need to say 'and she has no child', when 'as in her youth' already blocks even a pregnant בת כהן from תרומה?
steps.simpleTranslation: Why specifically a child? Even a fetus would also disqualify her. It is written 'as in her youth', which excludes a pregnant woman.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why the פסוק needs the words 'and she has no child'. ״כִּנְעוּרֶיהָ״ already shows that even a fetus stops her from eating תרומה, so a born child seems not worth mentioning. Steps 18-19 explain why both phrases are needed, and step 20 then returns to the משנה's wording.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same פסוק says she returns to her father's house 'as in her youth', and a pregnant woman is not in the state of her youth, so even a fetus disqualifies her. That makes the words 'and she has no child' look unnecessary, and the משנה's 'one day old' too. Steps 18-19 deal with the verses, and steps 20-22 deal with the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: Why specifically this? Why single it out?
A fetus
As in her youth
Excluding a pregnant woman

steps.whatToRemember: Both a born child and a fetus block a בת כהן from going back to eat תרומה. So the גמרא wants to know why the פסוק needs both 'no child' and 'as in her youth'.

phrases.english: Why specifically a child?
Even a fetus also disqualifies!
As it is written: "As in her youth",
phrases.notes: Same פסוק, ויקרא 22:13. She must come back in the same state as when she was a young girl.

phrases.english: excluding a pregnant woman.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי אִירְיָא זֶרַע? אֲפִילּוּ עוּבָּר נָמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks why the פסוק cited in the previous step needs the words 'no child', since 'as in her youth' already excludes even a pregnant woman.
steps.kashyaTarget: The words ״וְזֶרַע אֵין לָהּ״ in ויקרא 22:13, and with them the משנה's choice of a born child.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: 'As in her youth' already excludes a pregnant woman, so even a fetus disqualifies her. Then why does the פסוק need to say 'and she has no child'? The same problem also hits the משנה's 'one day old'.

steps.title: Both verses are needed: 'no child' alone would not cover a pregnant woman
steps.stepSummary: If the תורה had written only ״וְזֶרַע אֵין לָהּ״, we might think a child blocks her only because she became two bodies. A pregnant woman is still one body, so we would let her eat. That is why ״כִּנְעוּרֶיהָ״ is needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: Both are needed. If the תורה had written only 'and has no child', I would say she is blocked because at first she was one body and now there are two bodies. But here, at first one body and now still one body, I would say she may eat. So the תורה wrote 'as in her youth'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question of why we need two פסוקים. It starts by showing what ״כִּנְעוּרֶיהָ״ adds that ״וְזֶרַע אֵין לָהּ״ could not teach.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With only ״וְזֶרַע אֵין לָהּ״, the reason for the rule would seem to be 'one body became two bodies'. A pregnant woman has not yet become two separate bodies, so that reason would not apply to her. ״כִּנְעוּרֶיהָ״ is needed to block her too.

keyTerms.meaning: Both are necessary; each source teaches something the other could not
The Merciful One, meaning the תורה
'And she has no child' (ויקרא 22:13)
One body / two bodies
I might say she may eat

phrases.notes: 'At first' means back when she was single, before she married.

steps.terutzMaskana: ״כִּנְעוּרֶיהָ״ is needed to block the pregnant woman

steps.title: And 'as in her youth' alone would not cover a woman who already gave birth
steps.stepSummary: If the תורה had written only ״כִּנְעוּרֶיהָ״, we might think she is blocked only because her body is 'full'. After the birth her body is 'empty' again, so we would let her eat. That is why ״וְזֶרַע אֵין לָהּ״ is also needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if the תורה had written only 'as in her youth', I would say she is blocked because at first her body was empty and now it is full. But here, empty at first and empty now, I would say she may eat. So both are necessary.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the answer by showing the other direction: what ״וְזֶרַע אֵין לָהּ״ adds that ״כִּנְעוּרֶיהָ״ could not teach.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ״כִּנְעוּרֶיהָ״ means she must come back just as she was when young. A pregnant woman is not like that, because her body is 'full'. But once the baby is born her body is 'empty' again, like in her youth, so ״וְזֶרַע אֵין לָהּ״ is needed to block her because of the child.

keyTerms.meaning: 'As in her youth' (ויקרא 22:13), meaning she returns in the same state as before
An empty body, not pregnant
A full body, pregnant
It is necessary; closes the proof that both sources are needed

steps.whatToRemember: Each פסוק covers a different case. ״כִּנְעוּרֶיהָ״ blocks a pregnant בת כהן, and ״וְזֶרַע אֵין לָהּ״ blocks one who already has a child.

phrases.english: And if the Merciful One had written only 'as in her youth',
I would say that is because at first her body was empty
and now her body is full,
but here, where at first her body was empty
phrases.notes: 'Here' now means after she has already given birth.

phrases.english: and now her body is empty again,
I would say she may eat. So both are necessary.

steps.terutzHavaAmina: With only 'as in her youth', a woman who already gave birth would be allowed to eat, since her body is empty again

steps.title: The verses are settled, but why does the משנה say 'one day old'?
steps.stepSummary: The verses are explained, but a question about the משנה is still open. If even a fetus blocks a בת כהן from תרומה, why does the משנה say a one-day-old baby?
steps.simpleTranslation: The verses are answered. But in the משנה, why say specifically 'a one-day-old'? Even a fetus does the same!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא closes the question about the verses and goes back to its difficulty with the wording of the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We just learned from ״כִּנְעוּרֶיהָ״ that pregnancy already blocks her. So the משנה's words 'a one-day-old' seem to say too little, since an unborn baby already has this effect.

keyTerms.meaning: The verses have been answered
Why specifically this? (a question about why a detail was chosen)
A fetus, an unborn baby

phrases.english: The verses have been answered,

steps.title: רב ששת: the case is a כהן's son from a divorced wife
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת explains that the משנה is not talking about a בת כהן at all. It is talking about a כהן with two wives, one of them a גרושה. He has kosher sons from the other wife and a one-day-old son from the גרושה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת said: What case are we dealing with? A כהן who has two wives, one divorced and one not divorced. He has sons from the one who is not divorced, and a one-day-old son from the divorced one.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת answers the question by setting up a different case for the משנה. The ruling for this case comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A כהן may not marry a גרושה, so a son born from her is a חלל and not a כהן. Moving the משנה to this case means 'one day old' is no longer about the בת כהן rule, where a fetus already counts.

keyTerms.meaning: What case are we dealing with here? Used to set the text in a specific case
A divorced woman, whom a כהן may not marry
Son of a כהן from a forbidden marriage; he is not a כהן and may not eat תרומה

steps.confusionAlert: The other sons here are fully kosher כהנים. Only the baby from the גרושה is the problem, and the next step explains why.

phrases.english: Rav Sheshet said:
What case are we dealing with here?
A כהן who has two wives,
one divorced and one not divorced,

phrases.english: and he has a one-day-old son from the divorced one.

steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה's 'one day old' refers to a בת כהן's child, where a fetus already counts
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה refers to a כהן's son who is a חלל, born from a גרושה

steps.title: That baby stops his father's slaves from eating תרומה, but a fetus does not
steps.stepSummary: The one-day-old חלל son stops his father's slaves from eating תרומה. The משנה says 'one day old' to reject רבי יוסי, who holds that even a fetus does this. So a born baby does, and a fetus does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: He disqualifies his father's slaves from eating תרומה. This comes to exclude the view of רבי יוסי, who said a fetus also disqualifies. The משנה teaches us: a one-day-old, yes; a fetus, no.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת finishes his answer. He gives the ruling for his case and explains why the משנה chose the words 'one day old'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The slaves belong to the כהן's estate. A חלל son, once born, has a share in them, so they can no longer eat תרומה. In this case a fetus does not count, so 'one day old' is exactly right, and it rejects רבי יוסי.

keyTerms.meaning: Disqualifies, makes someone unable to eat תרומה
His father's slaves
To exclude, to reject a different opinion
This teaches us (what the text comes to say)

steps.whatToRemember: For a בת כהן, even pregnancy blocks תרומה. For a כהן's slaves, only a חלל son who is already born blocks them. That is why the משנה says 'one day old', against רבי יוסי.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that a fetus can count in one area of law and not in another. The משנה's exact wording is chosen to take sides in a מחלוקת.

steps.title: From whom does the baby inherit, and to whom does he pass it on?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes 'נוחל ומנחיל' from the משנה. It first suggests that the baby inherits from his father and passes it on to his brother from the same father.
steps.simpleTranslation: He inherits and he bequeaths. He inherits from whom? From his father. And he bequeaths to whom? To his brother from his father.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next phrase of the משנה and asks who the baby inherits from and who inherits from him. It gives a first guess, and this sets up the challenge in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The simple reading is that the father died, and the baby inherited him. Then the baby died, and his paternal brother inherited the baby. This is only a first try, and the גמרא will attack it right away.

keyTerms.meaning: inherits (receives property as an heir)
bequeaths (passes property on to his own heirs)
his brother from the same father (a paternal brother)

phrases.english: He inherits and he bequeaths.
He inherits — from whom? From his father.

To his brother from his father.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the תרומה clause of the משנה to its inheritance clause.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Who does the baby inherit from, and who are his heirs?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: First suggestion: he inherits from his father and passes it to his paternal brother.

steps.title: The brother would get the father's property anyway
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the first reading. The paternal brother inherits the father whether or not the baby is in the middle, so there is nothing new here.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he wants, let him inherit from his father, and if he wants, let him inherit from the baby!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the reading from step 23. It says the משנה would be teaching nothing new.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under that reading, the property ends up with the same brother either way. He gets it straight from the father, or he gets it through the baby. So the baby's status as an heir changes nothing, and the משנה would have no reason to mention it.

keyTerms.meaning: if he wants (either way, it makes no difference)
let him inherit

steps.kashyaTarget: The reading that the baby inherits from his father and passes it to his paternal brother.

steps.title: The baby inherits his mother and passes it to his father's sons
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת explains that the baby inherits his mother's property. Then he passes it on to his brothers from his father.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת said: He inherits his mother's property, so that he can pass it on to his brothers from the father.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת answers the challenge. He changes whose property we are talking about: it is the mother's, not the father's.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His brothers from the father are not the mother's sons, so they could never inherit from her directly. Because the baby inherited her property, it now passes through him to them. That is a real difference, so the משנה is teaching something.

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that being alive even one day makes the baby a real heir. That status can move property to a different family line.

steps.terutzMaskana: It means the mother's property, which reaches the paternal brothers only through the baby.

steps.title: Only a born baby inherits like this, not a fetus
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת adds a limit. Only a baby who was born, even one day old, does this. A fetus does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: And this applies specifically to a one-day-old baby, but not to a fetus.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת explains why the משנה says 'one day old.' He limits the rule to a baby who has been born.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A fetus whose mother died before it came out does not inherit her. So it also cannot pass her property to its paternal brothers. The reason comes in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: specifically, only
a fetus (not yet born)

phrases.english: And specifically a one-day-old,
but a fetus — no.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְדַוְקָא בֶּן יוֹם אֶחָד, אֲבָל עוּבָּר לָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues רב ששת's explanation by limiting it to a born baby.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only a baby who has been born inherits his mother and passes it on. A fetus does not.

steps.title: Why a fetus cannot inherit its mother
steps.stepSummary: The reason: we assume the fetus died first, and a son who is already dead cannot inherit his mother.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason? Because the fetus dies first, and a son does not inherit from his mother after he himself has died.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why a fetus is different and answers right away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When a pregnant woman dies, we assume the fetus inside her died before she did. A son who died before his mother never becomes her heir, so nothing can pass through him to his paternal brothers. A baby who was born and alive when she died did inherit, and he can pass it on.

keyTerms.meaning: what is the reason?
dies first
the son does not inherit his mother (here: once he has died)

steps.whatToRemember: A one-day-old baby who outlives his mother inherits her and passes her property to his paternal brothers. A fetus does not, because we assume it died first, and a son who died first does not inherit his mother.
steps.confusionAlert: Normally a son does inherit his mother. The rule here is about a son who died before her: he cannot become her heir and then pass it on.

phrases.english: What is the reason?
Because he dies first,
phrases.notes: 'He' is the fetus. We assume it died before its mother did.

phrases.english: and a son does not inherit from his mother.
phrases.notes: The sentence continues on the next amud: 'in the grave, to pass it on to his brothers from the father.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reason for the limit in step 26.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why does a fetus not inherit its mother?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: We assume it died first, and a son who died first does not inherit his mother.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Only a born baby, even one day old, can inherit his mother and pass it to his paternal brothers.
